headline: China's Talatan PV Park Pioneers Win-Win Model of Clean Energy and Ecological Restoration
article:
GONGHE, Qinghai (Xinhua) -- The Talatan photovoltaic (PV) park in Gonghe county, northwest China's Qinghai Province, has transformed from a windswept, degraded landscape into a thriving hub of clean energy and ecological restoration. By pioneering an integrated agrivoltaics model, the region demonstrates how solar power generation and animal husbandry can coexist to drive rural revitalization.

Stretching across more than 300 square kilometers, the park presents a striking visual contrast. Rows of deep blue solar panels capture the abundant high-altitude sunlight, while beneath them, resilient grasses have taken root. Flocks of sheep now graze peacefully under the panels, turning what was once a barren expanse into a productive ecosystem.

For local residents, this transformation has brought tangible changes to their daily lives. Yehdor, a local herder, recalled the hardships of the past. "Forage was scarce in the past," he said, explaining that desertification had severely limited grazing capacity. Today, the microclimate created by the solar arrays has revitalized the land, and Yehdor now grazes his sheep directly within the park.

The success of the Talatan model lies in its carefully designed ecological mechanism. The extensive solar panels significantly reduce wind speed and minimize soil moisture evaporation, creating favorable conditions for vegetation recovery. As the grass grew taller, it initially posed a challenge by shading the panels and increasing fire risks. The introduction of grazing sheep provided an elegant, natural solution. The sheep consume the excess forage, maintaining optimal grass height for solar efficiency while providing high-quality feed for the livestock.

This symbiotic relationship has turned the area into a major center for green development. The park's vast scale and favorable environment have attracted over 60 solar energy companies, establishing a robust industrial cluster.

Ultimately, the Talatan PV park illustrates a win-win approach to sustainable development. By seamlessly combining clean energy production with desertification control and livelihood improvement, the project offers a verifiable, replicable blueprint for ecological restoration in arid and semi-arid regions worldwide.
